motto: Designed from the published record, not from our own numbers
stage_note: System 08 is finished and will not be restarted. It made money in eight of eight research years and lost 26.1% in the sealed 2026, because the ranking inverted: the top-quarter-minus-bottom-quarter holding-period spread ran +2.3% to +5.9% per cycle every research year and -1.79% in 2026. A 20,000-draw bootstrap of the strategy's own annual distribution then showed the mandate was never reachable - P(year >= +30%) = 43.9% even in the regime where it works. The experiment loop is stopped, its restart hook is retired, and nothing here is running. The full account and the fifteen refuted ideas are in research/system08/POSTMORTEM.md.
title: The Residual Book
author: win-opus-5
question: What is the best crypto trading system that current published knowledge can justify - and what does the evidence say about why its edge exists and who pays for it?
question_note: A design that cannot answer the second half is not a design. An edge with no identified loser is a measurement artefact waiting to be discovered.
freeze_rule: A frozen design goes to the OPERATOR for review, never straight to code. Only after he agrees the theory do we download and normalise data and begin building.
claim: Hold the idiosyncratic component of an altcoin book and refuse the factor that comes attached to it. Published work says crypto is one asset wearing many tickers, and that in equities removing factor exposure from a momentum book produced the largest reduction in crash risk and drawdown. That operation, applied to the asset class that carries the most factor, is the design.
loser: Retail flow that is momentum-chasing SPECIFICALLY in crypto - the same traders are contrarian in stocks and gold - leveraged, and amplified by copy-trading platforms that measurably increase risk taking. They buy an altcoin for a narrative reason and acquire factor exposure they never priced, because it is a ratio of volatilities rather than a number on a screen. They keep paying because the capital that would compete it away is segmented by capital controls and regulation, and because the behaviour is a documented preference rather than an error to be learned out of.

established.title: Crypto is one asset wearing many tickers
established.finding: The common component of signed volume explains about 80% of bitcoin returns; a separate retail-universe study finds correlations better described by an isotropic model than by dispersed factor loadings.
established.consequence: Any long altcoin book is mostly a Bitcoin position that has not been priced as one. This is the structural fact the design has to answer.

established.title: The cross-section has a small, working factor model
established.finding: Three factors - market, size, momentum - capture the crypto cross-section; ten characteristics forming significant long-short strategies are all absorbed by it, and the core factors keep explaining variation post-2020.
established.source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu, Journal of Finance 2022
established.consequence: There is a defensible published definition of the factor to hedge, and it is not a private construction of ours.

established.title: Crypto anomalies mostly do not survive
established.finding: A re-examination of 49 crypto anomalies finds only 13 still significant over 2014-2023; crypto momentum evidence is described in the literature as inconclusive and methodology-dependent.
established.consequence: The base rate for a published crypto edge surviving is roughly one in four. This is the most important number on the page and it is not ours.

established.title: Residual momentum is the rare thing that replicated
established.finding: Running momentum on the residual after removing systematic factors gives significantly higher return-to-risk, greatly reduced crash risk, an almost doubled Sharpe ratio and the largest reduction in maximum drawdown; it is not explained by market, size, value, profitability, investment or total-return momentum, and it held up out of sample AFTER publication.
established.consequence: The credited mechanism is removing dynamic factor exposure - exactly the operation 2.1 says a crypto book most needs. Transferring this from equities to crypto is the central untested bet of the design, and it is named as such.

established.title: And it has now been tested on crypto - by the same people who killed the rest
established.finding: Li & Zhu use Iterative Double Selection LASSO over a large candidate set and arrive at a three-factor crypto model, DS3 = market + two-week momentum (MOM2) + RESIDUAL MOMENTUM (RMOM), reporting that it explains anomalies better than Liu/Tsyvinski/Wu's CPT3 or Bianchi & Babiak's IPCA3. It is the SAME paper as 2.3: the study that finds only 13 of 49 crypto anomalies still significant is the study that keeps residual momentum as one of the three factors it will admit.
established.source: Li & Zhu, Taming crypto anomalies: A Lasso-type factor model, RIBAF 2026
established.consequence: The equities-to-crypto transfer is no longer our untested assumption - someone else made it, on crypto, under selection pressure. It does NOT settle three things: a pricing factor is not a tradeable strategy (costs, capacity, turnover are outside what a factor model answers); their residual is defined against THEIR factor set, so which factor we neutralise is now a live design choice; and MOM2 is a two-week factor, which is a horizon statement our design has to answer.

established.title: Where the anomaly actually lives - and this constrains the design hard
established.finding: Crypto anomalies put through economic constraints: size, volume and distress come SOLELY from the 30-70% smallest coins; short-term reversal is driven mostly by low volume and low liquidity; momentum prevails in the LARGER cryptocurrencies but incurs substantial trading costs and extracts its alpha LARGELY FROM SHORT POSITIONS. Later period alphas are 9% to 76% lower than the first half.
established.source: Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, IRFA 2024
established.consequence: This changed the design rather than confirming it. Size and reversal are OUT on capacity - they live below our USD 10M turnover floor. Momentum is the one that survives where we can actually trade. And the SHORT SIDE IS MANDATORY, which is what makes the 2026-09-08 lifting of long-only load-bearing and retrospectively explains why six long-only systems could not capture it.

established.title: Cross-domain delivers explanation, not signal
established.finding: The multifractal and Hurst literature is real and replicated AS A DESCRIPTION of crypto price series. No peer-reviewed demonstration exists of a Hurst- or multifractal-derived rule surviving realistic costs out of sample; the trading applications are practitioner posts, and they founder on arbitrary thresholds and on re-trading every shift in the exponent.
established.source: O4 sweep of the multifractal / Hurst / adaptive-efficiency literature
established.consequence: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis stays as the best EXPLANATION of why edges decay - this lab's own history. Hurst may enter only as a state variable to argue about. Nothing from the cross-domain literature enters the signal slot. Closing this front is worth as much as opening one.

established.title: We can name the loser, and it is crypto-specific
established.finding: Retail traders are contrarian in stocks and gold but follow a momentum-like strategy in cryptocurrencies - the same traders, opposite behaviour. Copy-trading followers take more risk than they otherwise would and overreact when the signal provider does.
established.source: Kogan, Makarov, Niessner & Schoar, JFE 2024; Copy Trading, Management Science
established.consequence: The counterparty is a leveraged, momentum-chasing, socially amplified retail flow. That is who pays for the hedge - sourced, not asserted.

established.title: Why the edge is allowed to persist
established.finding: Arbitrage deviations across crypto venues are large, recurrent and larger across countries than within them, sustained by capital controls and regulatory segmentation rather than transaction costs. The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis frames inefficiency as competed away at a speed set by how much capital can reach it.
established.source: Makarov & Schoar, JFE 2020; AMH tested on high-frequency crypto, IRFA 2019
established.consequence: 'Capital cannot freely get there' is a real reason an edge persists. 'Nobody noticed' is not.

properties: It is the operation the literature credits for the doubled Sharpe - removing dynamic factor exposure - applied to the asset class that carries the most of it.

It attacks drawdown directly. The largest reported effect in the residual-momentum literature is on maximum drawdown and crash risk, and the operator's mandate names drawdown as an objective to minimise.
It requires the short side. The book cannot be factor-neutral without shorting the factor. Long-only was lifted on 2026-09-08; no earlier system here could express this.

open_slot.adopted: s = cross-sectional momentum of the residual, on LARGE-CAPITALISATION crypto only, expressed LONG AND SHORT.
open_slot.why_empty: It was held empty on purpose until the container was agreed, because filling the signal first is how this lab produced six systems that failed in the same year. It is now filled, and it was filled BY ELIMINATION AGAINST PUBLISHED CONSTRAINTS rather than by preference: reversal and size were rejected on capacity, cross-domain on the absence of any cost-surviving rule, and residual momentum is what was left standing.
constraints: Large caps only - 2.6: the tradeable version of momentum lives there, and the micro-cap anomalies are outside our USD 10M turnover floor anyway.
The short side is MANDATORY - 2.6: the alpha is extracted largely from short positions. A long-only book cannot express this at all.

Turnover is the enemy - 2.6 reports substantial trading costs and DS3's momentum factor is a two-week one. The design must be slow, and the horizon is pointed at by evidence rather than swept as a parameter.
Expect decay - 2.6 reports later-period alphas 9-76% lower and the AMH says that is the normal fate of a known edge. The design is built to be RETIRED, not defended.
open_slot.still_a_choice: Which factor set the residual is taken against - Bitcoin alone, CPT3, or DS3. 2.5 warns the residual is defined by its factor set. This is the first decision of implementation, registered here as a decision rather than smuggled in as a default.

kills.what: The factor is not hedgeable out of sample
kills.detail: If a loading estimated on past data does not neutralise future returns, the book is a directional bet wearing a hedge - worse than an honest directional bet.

kills.what: The residual is not ownable often enough
kills.detail: The mandate is a minimum +30% every calendar year. An architecture that cannot clear zero in most years cannot host it.

kills.what: The hedge costs more than the residual pays
kills.detail: The short factor leg pays funding and rebalances as the loading drifts. If carry plus turnover exceeds what the residual yields, no signal rescues it.

kills.what: The signal does not survive the multiple-testing base rate
kills.detail: Any candidate must clear roughly t > 3 rather than 1.96 (Harvey, Liu & Zhu) and be reported with a deflated Sharpe ratio correcting for selection over the number of trials actually run (Bailey & Lopez de Prado). This kill is aimed squarely at this laboratory's own history: the probability of backtest overfitting describes exactly the failure mode of six systems dying in the same year.
The counterparty is behavioural. If retail crypto flow stops being momentum-chasing and leveraged, the payment stops and the design should be RETIRED rather than re-fitted.

open_fronts.question: Is there a NON-PRICE input with published predictive content in crypto - crowd positioning, social and copy-trading flow, on-chain, attention?
open_fronts.why: DEFERRED ON PURPOSE. It is not needed to build this design; it is the most promising direction for the NEXT version of the signal, and holding it back keeps a second idea in reserve rather than spending every hypothesis on the first system.

answered.question: Has residual / idiosyncratic momentum ever been tested on CRYPTO?
answered.answer: YES, and it survived - one of the three factors of DS3, selected by LASSO in the same study that killed 36 of 49 crypto anomalies.

answered.question: What does a continuously-held short factor leg cost?
answered.answer: It is PAID, not charged - crypto funding is structurally positive, so longs pay shorts and the hedge earns carry on average. This is the weakest-sourced claim on the page: see the caveat.
answered.source: market funding data, NOT a peer-reviewed full-cycle measure

answered.question: Which anomalies actually survive economic constraints?
answered.answer: MOMENTUM, in the large caps, with the alpha LARGELY ON THE SHORT SIDE. Size and reversal live in micro-caps and low-liquidity names we cannot trade. This front changed the design.
answered.source: Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, IRFA 2024

answered.question: Does the cross-domain literature deliver anything tradeable?
answered.answer: NO. Descriptive and replicated as description; no peer-reviewed rule survives realistic costs out of sample. Front closed.

weak_link: O2 is the least well-sourced claim on the page. The funding numbers behind 'the short leg is paid' come from market data providers, not from a peer-reviewed measurement across a full cycle - and they sit in tension with the closed carry trade, whose published Sharpe collapsed and turned negative in 2025, which is precisely a statement that the funding regime changed. If the short leg costs rather than pays, K3 is the kill that fires, on the design's own registered terms.
